comments.author: FlashMode
comments.body_html:
The difference is that Scope Tweak changes the resolution of the internal renderer (in the scope), at least it was before, what Scope Tweak does now, I do not know

DERP, on the contrary, changes the resolution of the external renderer (everything that is not in the optic scope), thereby it increases the frame rate (if you don’t have a bottleneck on CPU performance) without affecting the quality of the picture inside the optic scope

comments.author: FlashMode
comments.body_html: Thanks mate

comments.author: FlashMode
comments.body_html:
In general, yes, a slight bifurcation of the picture (due to the lowered resolution), can create the illusion of some kind of depth of field effect. But in general, you can safely use the full depth of field effect in Amands Graphics, the only thing, lower its effect to the lowest value

The strength of depth of field in Amands Graphics adjusts for the resolution of the image, the higher resolution is, the shallower the depth of field is, and vice versa, the lower resolution is, the greater the depth of field is

Since DERP lowers the resolution of the external rendering, the intensity of depth of field in Amands Graphics increases linearly, so the effect itself should be lowered to a minimum (preferably)

I’ve added a tip (at the very bottom) to the title page of my mod description that shows the recommended depth of field settings for Amands Graphics
